newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly firmer, gas oil trails.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly firmer, gas oil trails.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly firmer on Wednesday, but gas oil lagged the market. Naphtha held firm with several uncovered requirements seen from petrochemical end-users for paraffinic grades.
Prices were assessed around quotes cif high +$4 cif Med.

Traders said that Algeria's Skikda oil port, which has been closed since the middle of last week due to high winds, failed to open again today. The closure has already delayed at least three naphtha liftings.
Gasoline was firmer, preventing arbitrage to NWE where demand was even stronger, traders said.
Traders said that the market for premium unleaded material was balanced, but sloppy for inferior grades.
Gas oil eased in line with IPE futures and plentiful supply of Russian, Italian and other grades, traders said.
However, the arbitrage with northern Europe was almost open and this stopped premiums falling any further, they added.
One trader, offering a heating oil cargo at Nov +$6 cif Med, continued to talk the market lower.
Algerian low sulphur diesel cargoes were moving into a very tight market in northern Europe, where premiums for this grade reached $30 over November IPE.

High sulphur fuel oil was marginally higher, the stronger levels seemingly flattening trades. Dealers said the market was steady to a touch firmer and that people were coming to terms with the higher numbers.
Interest remains high for Romania's proposal to buy $160 million worth of fuel oil this winter, which at present prices would represent 1.2 million tonnes.
There was unconfirmed talk that a low sulphur cargo was sold at $130 fob NWE, which was viewed as high compared with the confirmed low sulphur M-40 done yesterday at $135 cif Milazzo.
